owner.description: Whose an added server is: a person's, an organization's, or Latere's. Latere's own services have none.

message.description: One fixed sentence for a person.

Inject.description: Where a server that takes a key is sent it.

return_to.description: Where the browser goes after the sign-in. One of Latere's own pages.

scopes.description: Scopes to ask for beside the ones granted before.

authorization_url.description: Where to send the person's browser to sign in.

State.description: `pending` until the sign-in is confirmed, `connected`, or `needs_reconnect` when the service stopped taking the credential.

effect.description: The effect the server's tool marks give the tool.

hidden.description: Whether a hidden mark names the tool.

bearer.description: A person's signed-in token from auth.latere.ai, addressed to api.latere.ai. A token from a key is refused.

info.description:
A person connects a service once, and Latere keeps the credential. These
routes list the services a person may connect, add an MCP server of
one's own, connect a service, finish and renew its sign-in or replace
its key, and list, read, rename and disconnect a person's connections.
A credential is never part of an answer: no route, list or error
carries one.

Every route takes a person's signed-in token addressed to
`api.latere.ai`. In their personal context a person reaches their own
connections and servers; in an organization's context, what they
connected there and the services the organization offers. A
connection or a server somebody else holds answers as one that does
not exist.

Every error is one object: a `code` to branch on, a fixed `message` for
a person, and `details` for a developer.
info.summary: The services a person connects once, which Latere's agents use without holding the credential.
info.title: Latere Connections

get.description: The caller's connections in the token's context, newest first.

parameters.description: Only this owner's connections. It narrows what the caller may see and never widens it.
parameters.name: owner

parameters.name: connector

parameters.description: Only the connections in this state.
parameters.name: state

post.description:
Starts a connection for the caller in the token's context. A
service whose people sign in answers `201` with the connection,
`pending`, and `authorization_url`, where the person's browser goes
to sign in. The sign-in waits 10 minutes. The service sends the
browser back to `return_to` with the connection's id and a one-time
code, and the confirm finishes the connection. Every one of
Latere's own services signs people in.

A server that takes a key, or needs nothing, is connected at once:
the answer is the connection, `connected`. A key is given as
`credential.value`, tried against the server before it is kept, and
never answered. Such a connect names no `return_to`; one that does
is `400 invalid_field` with `details.reason` `no_sign_in`.

`return_to` is one of Latere's own pages, exactly: Latere Chat's
Connectors, `https://chat.latere.ai/settings/connectors`, or the
console's Connections, `https://platform.latere.ai/console/connections`.
Any other is `400 invalid_field`. In an organization's context, a
connect to a service the organization does not offer its members is
refused, `403 forbidden` with `details.reason` `not_chosen`; one it
offers is the member's own connection in that organization. A
server of an owner outside the token's context is
`404 connector_not_found`, and a server that is turned off is
`409 connector_disabled`.

201.description: The connection, or the connection pending with the address of its sign-in.

delete.description:
Deletes the connection and its credential at Latere, together.
Sessions stop using the service from their next message. At Google,
the access the person granted is removed when this was the last
connection of that Google account; at GitHub it is not revoked, and
the person removes it in their GitHub settings. In an organization,
its owners and admins may also delete a member's connection there.

patch.description:
Gives the connection a new name, unique among the owner's: a DNS
label of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 40
characters. An agent's session knows a connection by its name: it
is the name the agent is told, and `<NAME>_API_URL` in the session's
machine. A session takes a name that starts with a letter and has at
most 32 characters, so a rename to any other name is refused with
403 `forbidden` and `details.reason` `name_unusable`, and the
connection keeps its name.

get.description: The records of the requests an agent's sessions made through the connection, newest first, kept 30 days. A record says that a request happened, never what it said.

post.description:
Finishes a sign-in with the one-time code the browser brought back to
`return_to`, within 2 minutes of its return. Check first that the
`connection` the browser brought is one the person's own session
started. A wrong code is `400 invalid_code` and spends the sign-in; a
sign-in whose time has passed is `410 flow_expired`. Either way,
connect again.

put.description: A new key for a connection to a server that takes one. It replaces the old one in one write, and a connection that needed to be connected again is connected. The key is never answered.

post.description:
Starts a new sign-in for a connection to a service whose people sign
in: to change its account or its scopes, or after the service
stopped taking its credential. It is confirmed as a connect is. The
connection keeps its id and its name, and its old sign-in carries
requests until the confirm. Scopes named are asked for beside the
ones granted before. A connection that takes a key, or needs
nothing, is `409 wrong_kind`.

200.description: The connection, pending, with the address of its sign-in.

get.description:
The tools an MCP server lists through this connection, asked each
time, with the effect the server's tool marks give each and whether
they hide it. It is how a server's tools are read before choosing
their marks, and it records no call. A connection to a service that
is not an MCP server is `409 wrong_kind`; one that cannot be used
now is `409 connection_not_connected`, as a session's call is.

The services the caller may connect: Latere's own, in the order of
its catalog, then the MCP servers added by their address, newest
first. In a personal context those are the caller's own servers and
the ones Latere added; in an organization's context, the
organization's servers and the ones Latere added. A connector says
what the service is and how a person gives access to it, never a
credential. A server the caller may change carries `connections`.

parameters.description: Only this owner's added servers; Latere's own services are listed whatever it says. It narrows what the caller may see and never widens it.
parameters.name: owner

post.description:
Adds an MCP server by its address. In a personal context the server
is the caller's own, and only they see and connect it. In an
organization's context only its owners and admins add one, for its
members; a member is refused `403 forbidden` with `details.reason`
`role_insufficient`. Its `url` is `https` on port 443, and a
credential for it goes to that host alone.

Before it answers, Latere asks the server how people sign in, with
no credential: a server that answers needs nothing (`none`), one
that names its protected resource metadata signs people in
(`oauth`), and one that refuses with no metadata takes a key
(`token`). Leave `auth` out to take the server's answer. An `auth`
the answer does not admit is `422 auth_mismatch`, a server that
does not answer as one that can be connected is
`422 server_unreachable`, and a server that signs people in and
offers Latere no way to identify itself is
`422 sign_in_unsupported`. `auth.client`, a sign-in client
registered at the server, is taken only from an organization's
owner or admin. One owner adds at most 50 servers; one more is
`409 connector_limit`.

delete.description: Removes an added server when no connection uses it, by whoever may change it; one in use is `409 connector_in_use`, and can be turned off instead. Latere's own services are not removed here.

parameters.description: The id of an added server.
parameters.name: ref

parameters.description: The name of one of Latere's services, `github`, `gmail`, `google-calendar` or `google-drive`, or the id of an added server.
parameters.name: ref

patch.description:
Changes an added server in place, from the next request on. A
person changes their own servers; an organization's owners and
admins change its servers. `title`, `description`, `icon`, `tools`,
`auth.scopes`, `disabled` and the secret of the server's own
sign-in client change; `name`, `kind`, `url`, `auth.type` and the
client's id do not, and naming another value is
`400 immutable_field`. A server that is turned off stays listed: a
connect to it is `409 connector_disabled`, a session's call through
a connection to it is `409 connection_not_connected` with
`details.reason` `connector_disabled`, and its connections and
their credentials are kept until it is turned on. Latere's own
services are not changed here.

parameters.description: The id of an added server.
parameters.name: ref
